stemMd: Which assumption most directly underlies the editor and translator's compromise?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Readers can differ in whether they want to interrupt the narrative to examine a translation decision.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Every reader will ignore all reference marks.

options.label: C
options.textMd: A note at the back changes the original diary's events.

options.label: D
options.textMd: No reader is interested in how words are translated.

explanationMd: Putting a marked note at the back preserves uninterrupted reading while allowing consultation. That design assumes both preferences can be accommodated in one edition.

distractorRationale.b: The compromise makes optional consultation available rather than assuming universal avoidance.
distractorRationale.c: The note explains a choice; it does not change events.
distractorRationale.d: This would remove the reason to include the note.
